summary: The sample implements the core pipeline: PubMed ingestion, chunking, embedding, storage of chunk documents with embedding vectors, creation of a cosmosSearch vector-diskann index, and a simple HTTP /query endpoint that runs server-side cosmosSearch k-NN and returns an LLM-generated answer plus grounded citations (pmid + year). Automated tests and small-data verification (dummy embeddings) ran in the dev environment. Remaining issues are mostly hygiene, documentation, LlamaIndex integration for the RAG agent, error handling, and infra/dependency pinning; none of the discovered problems made the sample non-functional for the verified, limited end-to-end checks, but several checklist items and best-practice guidance are partly or not met and should be fixed before publishing.

requirement_results.requirement: Implement the pipeline in Python with LlamaIndex, including an ingestion step that fetches PubMed abstracts for rare diseases (e.g. through the PubMed E-utilities API) and keeps each abstract's text, PubMed ID and publication year.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/ingest.py lines 24-35 (search_pubmed) and 38-61 (fetch_abstracts collects pmid, title, abstract, year).

requirement_results.requirement: Split each ingested abstract into text chunks with LlamaIndex and carry the source abstract's PubMed ID and year on every chunk as metadata.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/ingest.py lines 66-73 (attempt to use TokenTextSplitter) and lines 86-92 (chunk creation stores 'pmid' and 'year' and 'chunk_id').

requirement_results.requirement: Generate an embedding for each chunk with LlamaIndex's embedding integration and store the chunks with their embedding vectors as fields on documents in Azure DocumentDB (through LlamaIndex's Azure DocumentDB vector store integration or a MongoDB-compatible Python driver such as PyMongo).
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/ingest.py lines 95-108 (embed_texts uses openai.Embedding.create and attaches 'embedding' and 'model' fields); app/src/ingest.py lines 111-121 (upsert_chunks uses bulk_write to store documents with embedding field in sample_healthcare_17.pubmed_chunks).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Either use LlamaIndex's OpenAIEmbedding (or LlamaIndex vector-store adapter) in embed_texts, or document in README why direct OpenAI calls were used; change the code to call LlamaIndex's embedding API when you want a full LlamaIndex integration.

requirement_results.requirement: Create a cosmosSearch vector index (kind vector-ivf, vector-hnsw or vector-diskann) on the embedding field in code, with dimensions matching the embedding model's output and a similarity of COS, L2 or IP.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/create_index.py lines 11-18 (createIndexes runCommand with 'key': {'embedding':'cosmosSearch'} and cosmosSearchOptions: kind 'vector-diskann', dimensions from OPENAI_EMBEDDING_DIMS, similarity 'COS').

requirement_results.requirement: Answer a researcher question by embedding it and running the vector similarity search inside Azure DocumentDB with $search / cosmosSearch, ordering the retrieved chunks by the database's similarity score (semantic relevance).
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/app.py lines 34-36 (openai embedding of query) and lines 41-56 (aggregate pipeline with $search.cosmosSearch knn, projecting searchScore, and collecting results in order).

requirement_results.requirement: Expose a RAG agent built with LlamaIndex in Python that takes a researcher question, retrieves the semantically ranked chunks from Azure DocumentDB and generates an answer conditioned on those chunks.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/app.py composes 'context' from retrieved chunks and calls OpenAI ChatCompletion to produce an answer (lines 61-67), but it does not instantiate or use LlamaIndex retrieval/response agent primitives; LlamaIndex is only used for chunking.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Either (A) wire the retrieval step + prompt/LLM call into a LlamaIndex ServiceContext/LLMPredictor + Retriever pipeline, or (B) change sample description/README to state that retrieval is via direct cosmosSearch+ChatCompletion rather than a LlamaIndex-managed RAG object.

requirement_results.requirement: Include a citation for each retrieved abstract the answer draws on, and give the PubMed ID and abstract year in every citation.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/app.py lines 58-60 build Citation objects with pmid and year; the system prompt (line 63) instructs the LLM to cite PubMed IDs and years; QueryResponse includes citations (lines 27-29 and return at line 69).

requirement_results.requirement: The connection string and model credentials come from environment variables; none appear in the repository.
requirement_results.evidence: app/.env.example contains DOCUMENTDB_URI and OPENAI_API_KEY placeholders (app/.env.example lines 2-7); app/src/db.py reads DOCUMENTDB_URI (lines 8-19); app/src/app.py and app/src/ingest.py read OPENAI_API_KEY and embedding/model environment variables (app/src/app.py lines 9-12; app/src/ingest.py lines 14-17).

requirement_results.requirement: A .env.example lists every setting with placeholder values.
requirement_results.evidence: app/.env.example lists DOCUMENTDB_URI, OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL, OPENAI_EMBEDDING_DIMS, OPENAI_LLM_MODEL (app/.env.example lines 2-7).

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output.
requirement_results.evidence: Default embedding model and dims are set in .env.example and code: OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL 'text-embedding-3-small' and OPENAI_EMBEDDING_DIMS=1536 (app/.env.example lines 6-7); create_index.py uses the OPENAI_EMBEDDING_DIMS default to set index dimensions (app/src/create_index.py line 33 and lines 13-16).

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them for a larger one.
requirement_results.evidence: create_index.py sets 'maxDegree' and 'lBuild' defaults in code (app/src/create_index.py lines 17-18), but README.md does not document how to tune these parameters for different data sizes (app/README.md has index creation notes but no tuning guidance).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a short section in README.md describing the chosen defaults (maxDegree/lBuild), why they suit the small sample, and instructions + example values for tuning them for larger corpora (refer to documentdb-vector-search skill docs).

requirement_results.requirement: One database client is created and reused across requests.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/db.py implements a process-level singleton MongoClient with a thread Lock (lines 12-19 and get_client function lines 13-20).

requirement_results.requirement: A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data.
requirement_results.evidence: scripts/seed.py runs src.ingest; ingest.upsert_chunks uses UpdateOne with upsert=True to avoid duplicates (app/src/ingest.py lines 111-121). create_index.py can be run as a module and sets index dimensions idempotently (app/src/create_index.py lines 4-24).

requirement_results.requirement: /search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/app.py query handler performs no input validation (no empty-query check) and does not catch embedding or LLM exceptions (app/src/app.py lines 32-36 and 61-67).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add input validation and error handling in src/app.py: return 400 for empty query, and wrap embedding/LLM calls in try/except to return clear 5xx/4xx errors with a short message. Example: if not req.query.strip(): raise HTTPException(400, 'query is required').

requirement_results.requirement: Search results include the similarity score.
requirement_results.evidence: Aggregation pipeline projects {'score': {'$meta':'searchScore'}} and the Citation model includes score (app/src/app.py lines 54 and 20-25).

requirement_results.requirement: Dependencies are pinned in requirements.txt.
requirement_results.evidence: app/requirements.txt uses flexible minimum versions (e.g., 'llama-index>=0.9.0', 'pymongo>=4.5') instead of exact pinned versions (app/requirements.txt).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Pin critical dependencies to exact tested versions (e.g., 'llama-index==0.14.26', 'pymongo==4.20.1', 'openai==3.59.0') in requirements.txt or provide a constraints file; document why pins were chosen.

requirement_results.requirement: Unit tests run without a live cluster.
requirement_results.evidence: tests/test_chunking.py uses only local code paths and pytest passed in the build run (events.jsonl: '1 passed'). The ingest module imports are arranged to avoid external calls during that unit test (events.jsonl lines showing pytest success).

requirement_results.requirement: Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type.
requirement_results.evidence: The repository has no IaC files (no Bicep/Terraform/ARM templates) to provision Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters; README assumes an existing cluster (app/README.md lines 11-15).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a small IaC example (Bicep or Terraform/AzAPI) that creates a minimal Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters resource with low-cost defaults, or include an explicit note that the run environment must supply a cluster and link to the product quickstart for provisioning.

requirement_results.requirement: The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up.
requirement_results.evidence: README includes what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, seeding and run instructions (app/README.md lines 3-26) but lacks explicit clean-up steps to drop the created collection or delete resources (no clean-up section).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a 'clean-up' section to README.md with commands to drop the collection and guidance on how to delete the sample DB or the cluster if the user provisioned one.

requirement_results.requirement: The sample uses the name 'Azure DocumentDB' throughout, and no former or neighbouring product name.
requirement_results.evidence: README and code refer to 'Azure DocumentDB' and 'DocumentDB' (app/README.md lines 1 and 7; code comments consistent), no old Cosmos DB/RU naming appears in README text.

checks.practice: One client is created and reused for the life of the process.
checks.evidence: app/src/db.py lines 12-20 implement a singleton MongoClient and get_db(); created via get_client().

checks.practice: Enable the driver's retry settings and implement application-level retries with exponential backoff.
checks.evidence: app/src/db.py sets MongoClient(..., retryWrites=True) (app/src/db.py line 18) but ingest and index creation do not implement application-level retries or exponential backoff (app/src/ingest.py embed_texts/upsert_chunks and app/src/create_index.py have no retry wrappers).
checks.fix: Wrap critical data-plane operations (embed_texts calls, upsert_chunks bulk_write, create_vector_index runCommand) with an idempotent retry loop and exponential backoff (or use a retry decorator) and ensure bulk operations are idempotent (they already use upsert).

checks.practice: Never commit connection strings or keys to source control; read DOCUMENTDB_URI and other secrets from environment variables or a secrets store and ship a .env.example with placeholders.
checks.evidence: app/.env.example lists placeholders (app/.env.example lines 2-7) and code reads DOCUMENTDB_URI from env (app/src/db.py lines 8-19); no connection string found in source.

checks.practice: Store each text chunk as a separate document with explicit metadata fields (pmid / source_year / chunk_id / chunk_text / embedding).
checks.evidence: app/src/ingest.py chunk_texts produces {'pmid','year','chunk_id','text'} and embed_texts/upsert_chunks persist these with 'embedding' and 'model' fields (app/src/ingest.py lines 90-106 and 111-121).

checks.practice: Create a native vector index whose parameters match your embeddings exactly (kind: vector-diskann / vector-hnsw / vector-ivf) and set dimensions and similarity.
checks.evidence: app/src/create_index.py uses createIndexes runCommand with cosmosSearchOptions.kind='vector-diskann', dimensions from OPENAI_EMBEDDING_DIMS, similarity='COS' (app/src/create_index.py lines 11-18). The index was created successfully in the run (events.jsonl createIndexes result and documentdb_list_indexes output).

checks.practice: Run vector k-NN searches server-side with the $search aggregation stage and the cosmosSearch operator rather than scanning embeddings client-side.
checks.evidence: app/src/app.py pipeline uses $search.cosmosSearch.knn with 'path':'embedding' and returns results server-side (app/src/app.py lines 41-56).

checks.practice: Project/return the metadata you need (pubmed_id, year, chunk_id, snippet/text and searchScore) so each hit can be presented as a grounded citation without extra DB round-trips.
checks.evidence: Aggregation pipeline projects pmid, year, chunk_id, text and score via {'$project': {'pmid':1,'year':1,'chunk_id':1,'text':1,'score':{'$meta':'searchScore'}}} (app/src/app.py line 54).

checks.practice: Avoid N+1 reads by returning vector-search hits and required metadata/text in a single DB operation.
checks.evidence: app/src/app.py uses a single aggregation pipeline to retrieve search hits with metadata and text (app/src/app.py lines 41-56).

checks.practice: Create conventional (B-tree) indexes on fields you filter or sort on (e.g., pubmed_id, source_year).
checks.evidence: documentdb_list_indexes output shows only the default _id index and the embedding vector index; no index on 'pmid' or 'year' exists (events.jsonl documentdb_list_indexes result).
checks.fix: Create an index on 'pmid' and/or 'year' if the application will filter or sort by those fields. Example: db.command({'createIndexes':'pubmed_chunks','indexes':[{'key':{'pmid':1},'name':'idx_pmid'}]})

checks.practice: Choose a chunk size tuned to your embedding model and record chunk length/token count in metadata for debugging.
checks.evidence: The app uses chunk_size=512, chunk_overlap=50 in chunk_texts (app/src/ingest.py line 66) but there is no public guidance in the installed DocumentDB skill set prescribing chunk sizes; this practice came from prior knowledge.
checks.searched: Searched installed skills and Microsoft docs for 'Azure DocumentDB chunk size tokens' (no specific guidance found).
checks.fix: Document an explicit recommendation for default chunk_size and when to tune it. Add 'token_count' to stored metadata to enable later tuning experiments.
checks.what_would_help: A sentence in the sample README stating the recommended chunk_size for the chosen embedding model and how to change it, plus an example of recording token counts in metadata.

checks.practice: When ingesting many documents use batched bulk writes (driver bulk APIs) and moderate batch sizes.
checks.evidence: ingest.upsert_chunks uses coll.bulk_write(ops) to perform bulk upserts (app/src/ingest.py lines 111-121).
checks.searched: Searched installed skills for DocumentDB guidance on batch sizes; none found in the installed skill set.
checks.fix: Consider exposing a configurable batch_size for upsert_chunks and document recommended defaults in README.
checks.what_would_help: A short note in README describing recommended batch sizes for small vs large corpora and a pointer to the DocumentDB vector-search skill for index-build considerations.

decision_reviews.comment: Approval with operator reason and evidence 'Approved with --yes' is an operator action; the event is recorded (decisions.jsonl line 1) and is supported by the run log.
Choosing Python matches the sample prompt and the environment; events show Python tools used and code written in Python (events.jsonl records D002 and later Python files created).
Choosing PyMongo and implementing a singleton MongoClient is documented and implemented (app/src/db.py); events show the documentdb-driver skill was loaded before this decision was logged.

The decision to use OpenAI text-embedding-3-small is a 'model_default' choice (decisions.jsonl D004). It's defensible but not grounded in public DocumentDB guidance; the readiness report flagged model selection as an information gap. The code and .env.example use that default (app/.env.example and app/src/ingest.py), so the choice is internally consistent but should be reviewed by the owner for appropriateness in medical abstract retrieval.

Selecting gpt-3.5-turbo as the LLM is again a model_default decision (D005). Defensible for demonstrations, but it is not backed by product guidance and should be documented in README as an explicit default the user can change.
Data model choice (single denormalized 'pubmed_chunks' collection) matches the code (app/src/ingest.py upsert_chunks) and is consistent with the sample's access pattern.
Choosing vector-diskann is supported by the documentdb-vector-search skill and the index was created as vector-diskann in the run (events.jsonl shows index with kind 'vector-diskann').

The decision to avoid pinning llama-index (D008) contradicts the gallery checklist expectation that dependencies be pinned. The event log shows requirements.txt uses flexible minimums (events.jsonl write_file). This should be changed to pinned versions for reproducibility.
Choosing FastAPI is reasonable and implemented (app/src/app.py uses FastAPI).

Inserting dummy zero vectors to verify DB/index creation without external keys is a pragmatic 'model_default' decision (D010); the run log shows dummy docs were inserted successfully (events.jsonl run_command inserting dummy docs). The decision is justified and recorded.

Using the MCP server to create the index is reasonable (D011 references the readiness_report). The documented MCP call failed during the run due to management tools being disabled by default (events.jsonl shows ToolExecutionException with 'Management tools are disabled by default'). The decision was a reasonable attempt but contingent on an opt-in configuration; the tool failure is recorded in events.jsonl.
Falling back to PyMongo db.command(createIndexes) after MCP failure is sensible; events.jsonl shows the runCommand created the index successfully and the index is visible via documentdb_list_indexes.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No product-level guidance telling sample authors which embedding provider/model to choose and what default dimensions to assume for a PubMed-abstract LlamaIndex sample.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Installed documentdb-* skills and Microsoft Learn pages (see readiness_findings and skill resources loaded during the run).
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Builder made a model_default decision (text-embedding-3-small / 1536 dims). That is internally consistent, but agents working from memory may choose incompatible dims and create a mismatched index. The sample requires the user to keep the env dims and model aligned.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short guidance page 'Embedding model choices for DocumentDB samples' that: (1) lists recommended embedding models for small gallery samples with dims (e.g., OpenAI text-embedding-3-small: 1536), (2) explains that index dimensions must equal model output dims, (3) shows a code snippet to validate embedding length at runtime and fail fast or rebuild index, (4) advises how to change OPENAI_EMBEDDING_DIMS and re-run create_index.py.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: README lacks guidance on how to tune vector-index parameters (lBuild, maxDegree) for larger data sizes and trade-offs.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Repository README and installed skills; the vector-search skill documents parameters but the sample README doesn't surface tuning advice.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample uses conservative defaults but does not educate users how to scale the index for larger corpora; users may copy defaults that are suboptimal for production.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a subsection to the sample README titled 'Index tuning for larger datasets' linking to documentdb-vector-search SKILL.md and summarizing recommended maxDegree/lBuild ranges for small/medium/large corpora plus an example command showing how to re-create the index with new parameters.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No public DocumentDB guidance in the installed skills prescribes a chunk size tuned to embeddings/tokenization; this practice was prior knowledge only.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Searches in installed skills and Microsoft Learn (see discovered_practices notes).
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Builder picked chunk_size=512 and overlap=50 by convention; without explicit guidance maintainers may not choose an optimal chunk size for retrieval quality vs cost.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short note in the sample README advising a default token-based chunk size for the sample embedding model (e.g., ~512 tokens), why overlap matters, and a small script/flag to record token counts for each chunk to support tuning experiments.

doc_gaps.topic: Batch size guidance for bulk writes
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No public guidance in installed skills about recommended batch sizes for DocumentDB bulk writes for vector ingestion.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Installed skills and Microsoft Learn; searches for 'DocumentDB bulk_write batch size' returned no useful DocumentDB-specific guidance.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Ingest uses bulk_write but leaves batch sizing implicit; users might choose too-large batches for their cluster tier and experience timeouts or resource contention.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short 'Bulk ingestion' page in the docs or agent-kit describing recommended batch sizes (e.g., 500–2000 for high-throughput clusters, 100–500 for smaller tiers), recommendations to use ordered=False, and an example with PyMongo bulk_write and retry/backoff.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: The starter prompt and skills did not force the builder to implement explicit input validation and user-facing error messages for empty queries or failed embedding/LLM calls.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Repo code and installed skills; no sample-level rule enforced error-handling for the HTTP API.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The /query endpoint will raise unhandled exceptions for empty input or failed embedding/ChatCompletion calls, yielding unclear server errors to users.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add an agent-kit rule and a small README snippet requiring API endpoints to validate inputs and handle external-API exceptions clearly (HTTP 400 for empty queries, HTTP 502/503 for failed upstream embedding/LLM calls), plus a minimal try/except wrapper example for the openai embedding/ChatCompletion calls.

doc_gaps.topic: Dependency pinning policy for gallery samples
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No enforced sample-level policy or guidance requiring dependencies to be pinned to exact test-verified versions.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Repo and installed skills; README does not advise pinning and requirements.txt uses minimum versions.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The builder chose flexible minimum version constraints which reduces reproducibility and risks runtime incompatibilities in CI or on users' machines.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short agent-kit rule and README checklist item: 'Pin critical dependencies (llama-index, pymongo, openai) to test-verified exact versions in requirements.txt or provide a constraints file; update pins when intentionally upgrading and document test results.' Provide example pinned requirements and a brief procedure for updating pins.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A minimal Bicep/Terraform example to provision an Azure DocumentDB mongoClusters resource as part of the sample.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Repository and installed skills; README instructs using an existing cluster but provides no IaC artifact in repo.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample assumes an existing cluster; users who want to reproduce the demo need to consult external quickstarts and may select the wrong resource type (databaseAccounts vs mongoClusters).
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a minimal Bicep and Terraform example in a /infra folder that provisions a low-cost mongoClusters M-series cluster with variables for tier/region and a note: 'Use this only for development; billing applies'. Include an explicit note about using Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters (not databaseAccounts).

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: During the run the documentdb_create_index MCP tool failed with 'Management tools are disabled by default. Set ENABLE_MANAGEMENT_TOOLS=true to opt in.' There is no local repo note documenting that MCP management tools may be disabled by default and how to opt in.
doc_gaps.where_searched: events.jsonl and the repo README; the run captured the tool error but the README doesn't explain the opt-in flag.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The builder fell back to PyMongo runCommand to create the index; users expecting MCP-based index creation may see the same error and not understand the opt-in.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a short note in README.md under 'Index creation' explaining MCP management tools may be disabled and include the env note: 'If MCP management tools are disabled, set ENABLE_MANAGEMENT_TOOLS=true in the MCP server config or use the included create_index.py which uses the driver as a fallback.'

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Several build-time choices (embedding model, LLM model, and dependency pinning policy) were 'model_default' decisions rather than grounded in product docs.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Model_default decisions led to configuration choices (text-embedding-3-small, gpt-3.5-turbo, flexible requirements) that maintainers should review for correctness, especially for a biomedical sample.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add an agent-kit rule requiring explicit justification (in README or decisions.jsonl) when choosing a model_default for embedding/LLM/models or dependency pinning; require a short rationale and test notes for medical domain samples.
